newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs to observe silence for flood victims.
newsitem.headline: Czechs to observe silence for flood victims.

text.p: The Czech government asked citizens to observe one minute of silence at noon (1000 GMT) on Thursday in honour of the dozens of people who died in this month's floods in the east of the country.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus told a news conference during a government meeting east of Prague that production should stop for one minute as sirens and church bells sounded.
This month's floods, the worst of the century, claimed 48 victims in the Czech Republic and more than 50 in neighbouring Poland.
The flooding, which began with torrential rains, also brought havoc to parts of Poland, Slovakia and Austria and has now spread to eastern Germany.
Citizens in Poland observed a day of mourning last Friday, honouring the dead with flags at half mast and special church services, while public broadcasters played serious music.
Thousands have been left homeless in the disaster, and governments have been urgently trying to find funds for immediate relief and reconstruction.
